headline: The Game Archive Reaches 5,000 Magazines
lede: The Video Game History Foundation has made more than 5,000 magazines searchable—nearly 600,000 pages spanning four decades of game culture. Its next chapter turns east, adding Japanese-language scans, OCR, and volunteer-built indexes for researchers.

headline: Remembering Technology Chronicler Bob Cringely
lede: Mark Stevens, known to generations of readers as Bob Cringely, has died peacefully in his sleep. Through books and PBS documentaries including Triumph of the Nerds, he made the personal-computer industry legible to a broad audience.

headline: The Platform Already Knows How
lede: Developers keep rebuilding capabilities that browsers, databases, and operating systems already provide. The reasons are historical and practical—bad documentation, old incompatibilities, framework momentum—but native knowledge remains one of the cheapest ways to reduce complexity.
pullquote: Before building another abstraction, learn what the platform already does.

headline: The Tradeoff Behind Trade Work
lede: The skilled-trades boom is less universal than its shorthand suggests. Pay, credentials, competition, injury, and automation vary sharply by occupation, making career advice that treats every trade alike analytically unsound.

headline: Old AMD GPUs Get New Linux Life
lede: Valve engineer Timur Kristóf is moving decade-old GCN hardware onto AMDGPU, bringing better Vulkan support, power management, and display handling. The kernel work reportedly delivers gains near 30 percent while extending the useful life of cards their maker has largely left behind.

headline: France Blocks Access to Rodin’s Digital Doubles
lede: After eight years of litigation, France’s highest administrative court ruled that publicly funded 3D scans of Rodin sculptures need not be released under freedom-of-information law. The decision leaves a public-domain collection behind an institutional gate, with the activist who sought access ordered to pay €3,000.

headline: Agents Need Documents, Not Vague Memories
lede: Conversation snippets and vector retrieval can preserve context without preserving understanding. A document-based workspace—plain Markdown, explicit decisions, versioned instructions—offers agents something quieter and more auditable: a shared record of how the work is supposed to proceed.

headline: Hole Punch Bends Space Into a Puzzle
lede: In this browser game, you do not steer the spaceship; you place black holes and let gravity draw the route. Limited matter, hazards, and increasingly elaborate fields turn orbital mechanics into a compact experiment in trial, error, and delight.

headline: Jagex Announces a New RuneScape MMO
lede: RS4 is in development in Unreal Engine and will begin in Ashenfall, within the Gielinor universe. It will stand alongside RuneScape, Old School RuneScape, and Dragonwilds, with release timing, platforms, and monetization still unspecified.

headline: gpuvis Turns GPU Traces Into Timelines
lede: gpuvis is an open-source visualizer for inspecting GPU and system-performance traces. Built around SDL, Dear ImGui, and OpenGL support, it gives graphics developers a clearer view of scheduling, synchronization, and bottlenecks.
